prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell) coordinates Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport; integrates regional flow management/Airport Collaborative Decision-Making. Elements: Demand Prediction Service/Capacity Assessment Module/Slot Allocation Engine/Airport CDM Portal/Digital Briefing Room/Tower Sequence Manager/Ramp Movement Board/Departure Metering Service/Arrival Regulation Console/Contingency Operations Console/Weather Ingest Gateway/Flight Data Exchange/Surface Surveillance Adapter/Airline Interface Adapter/Alert Distribution Hub/Performance Analytics Warehouse/Audit Event Ledger/Identity Access Service/Business Rules Registry/Time Synchronization Service/Common Situation Display. Indicators: North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter/East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor/Sector Load Monitor/Gate Conflict Detector. Actors: Regional Flow Manager/Airline Operations Coordinator/Network Operations Liaison/Aircraft Operator Representative/Slot Coordinator/Tower Supervisor/Ramp Control Lead/Airport Duty Manager/Ground Handling Dispatcher/Handling Resource Planner/Deicing Coordinator/Meteorology Briefing Officer/Airspace Sector Planner/Military Airspace Liaison/Emergency Response Coordinator/Data Governance Steward/System Support Engineer. Modes: Normal Operations/Adverse Weather Mode/Capacity Reduction State/Recovery Phase/Contingency Fallback State/Slot Compliance State. Reduced capacity requires rapid Tactical Regulation Proposal/consistent Ground Delay Program; recovery monitors Target Off Block Time/Calculated Takeoff Time/compliance. Morning baseline precedes bank-locking; Regional Flow Manager owns horizon/cutover/checkpoints. Flight Data Exchange normalizes Flight Intent Message/schedules; Demand Prediction Service produces demand. Weather Ingest Gateway preserves outlook issue-time; Airspace Sector Planner declares constraints; Military Airspace Liaison confirms assumptions/uncertainty. Tower Supervisor sends Runway Inspection Note before consolidation; declares configuration/length/sequencing. Airport Duty Manager confirms facilities/services. Ramp Control Lead reviews board/sensors; Ground Handling Dispatcher confirms coverage; Handling Resource Planner flags resource-limited turns/stands. Capacity Assessment Module combines declarations/weather/airspace/stands/resources into proposed Airport Acceptance Rate, tested against demand. Slot Coordinator prepares feasibility without binding Calculated Takeoff Time; Departure Metering Service estimates provisional Target Off Block Time sensitivity; Arrival Regulation Console highlights inbound interventions. Digital Briefing Room displays Airport Capacity Plan/logs unresolved assumptions in Collaborative Decision Log. Common Situation Display shares approved baseline; Alert Distribution Hub announces approval/controlled changes. Performance Analytics Warehouse retains inputs/declarations/approval-times for Post Operations

New part:
S075: Section 4 defines the accountable roles used after the approved morning baseline is distributed through the Regional Flow Platform.
S076: For role-call clarity, the Regional Flow Manager is also known as Copperfin during this deployment.
S077: During pre-tactical operations, the Regional Flow Manager owns the regional operating intent and confirms that planned demand, declared capacity, and coordination milestones are aligned.
S078: The Regional Flow Manager reviews the Airport Capacity Plan, the Ground Delay Program status, and any Tactical Regulation Proposal before they are presented for collaborative agreement.
S079: The Airspace Sector Planner supports the Regional Flow Manager by validating sector constraints in the Sector Load Monitor and by advising whether demand smoothing is required before tactical execution.
S080: The Slot Coordinator maintains accountability for Calculated Takeoff Time allocation policy and confirms that the Slot Allocation Engine applies the current Business Rules Registry parameters.
S081: The Airline Operations Coordinator represents carrier operating priorities and confirms that Flight Intent Message updates are complete, timely, and traceable.
S082: The Aircraft Operator Representative provides aircraft-specific constraints when requested and is responsible for ensuring that operator commitments entered in the Airport CDM Portal are operationally achievable.
S083: The Network Operations Liaison coordinates with adjacent network units and confirms that regional measures remain compatible with upstream and downstream flow constraints.
S084: The Network Operations Liaison also records external coordination outcomes in the Collaborative Decision Log so that later decisions can be reconstructed without relying on informal communications.
S085: The Meteorology Briefing Officer produces the Storm Cell Snapshot before the pre-tactical capacity review begins.
S086: The Meteorology Briefing Officer briefs forecast confidence, timing risk, and expected operational impact in the Digital Briefing Room using data supplied through the Weather Ingest Gateway.
S087: When forecast uncertainty is material, the Meteorology Briefing Officer states the trigger conditions that would justify moving from Normal Operations to Adverse Weather Mode.
S088: The Airport Duty Manager is the primary airport escalation contact and confirms that airport-side constraints are reflected consistently across the Airport CDM Portal and the Common Situation Display.
S089: The Tower Supervisor is accountable for tactical runway sequencing decisions and confirms that the Tower Sequence Manager reflects the current runway configuration.
S090: The Ramp Control Lead is accountable for apron movement coordination and maintains the Ramp Movement Board in a state that supports reliable departure metering.
S091: The Ground Handling Dispatcher confirms that handling resource assumptions are current in the Handling Resource Planner and escalates material deviations through the Airport Duty Manager.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
